subject: general
question: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum which is invested for 5 years at a certain rate per cent p. a. is Rs. 9,800 and the amount payable on the same sum invested for 10 years at the same rate is Rs. 12,600. If simple interest is offered in both cases, the rate of interest p. a. is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple interest remains constant for every year.

SI for 5 years = A₁₀ − A₅ = 12600 − 9800 = ₹2800

Principal (P) = A₅ − SI for 5 years = 9800 − 2800 = ₹7000

SI for 1 year = 2800 ÷ 5 = ₹560

Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ P) × 100 = (560 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 5 years (A₅) = ₹9800

Amount after 10 years (A₁₀) = ₹12600

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
